sentences.text:
This third application has been filed by the applicant under Section 483 of BNSS, 2023 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No. 339/2023, registered at Police Station - Susner District Agar Malwa(M.P.) for offence punishable under Sections 363, 376, 3763(2)(n), 376(3), 365, 344 of IPC,
and Sections 3/4, 5(l)/6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.

entities.text: Police Station - Susner District Agar Malwa(M.P.)
entities.label: ORG

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Applicant is in judicial custody since 29.11.2024.
His first bail application was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 07.05.2025, passed in M.Cr.C. No.15989/2025.
His second bail application has been dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 10.11.2025, passed in M.Cr.C. No.42481/2025 with liberty to renew the prayer for bail after one month.
2. Learned counsel for the applicant in addition to the grounds mentioned in the petition submitted that as per the evidence on record, the victim was major at the time of alleged incident.
Learned counsel further 2 MCRC-57970-2025 submitted that the victim and her father had stated different dates of the incident in their evidence, therefore prosecution is doubtful.
All material prosecution witnesses have been examined.
Applicant is aged around 21 years.
The trial Court did not conclude the trial despite last order dated 10.11.2025 granting liberty of one month to renew the prayer.
The trial would take time to conclude.
Therefore, the applicant be extended the benefit of bail.

3. Per contra, learned counsel for the State submitted that the victim in her initial statement recorded under Section 183 of BNSS at the evidence before the trial Court made specific allegation of penetrative sexual assault against the applicant.
The DNA examination report substantiates the allegation of penetrative sexual assault.
As per the scholar register, the victim was aged around 15 years and 7 months at the time of the alleged incident.
The trial has concluded and the matter is at Sanju @ Sanjulal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4840471/

sentences.text: 1 advance stage of defence evidence, which is pending for consideration of the application filed by the applicant, therefore, delay is not attributable to the prosecution.
The trial would conclude shortly.

4. Heard both the parties and perused the record.
5.
As per accusation applicant Suraj @ Sanjulal aged around 22 years kidnapped the minor victim aged around 15 years and 7 months and subjected her to penetrative sexual assault.
Victim P.W.1 in her evidence before the trial Court alleged kidnapping, wrongful confinement and rape on multiple occasions against the applicant.
The allegation of penetrative sexual assault is duly corroborated by medial and DNA examination report.
3 MCRC-57970-2025 Age of the victim is verified by Anil Jain (Headmaster) P.W.3- by submitting the scholar register before the trial Court.
The Prosecution evidence is completed and the matter is pending for defence evidence, therefore, trial is not unnecessarily delayed.
6. Considering these aspects of the matter, this Court is of the considered opinion that applicant does not deserves to be released on bail.
7. Consequently, the bail application (MCRC No.57970 of 2025) is dismissed.
(SANJEEV S KALGAONKAR) JUDGE sumathi Sanju @ Sanjulal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4840471/
